title: The dental team & the wider NHS
blurb: The seven GDC-registered titles, the roles that aren't registered, and how dental care links into the wider NHS.
question: On your first day at a new practice you meet a dentist, a hygienist, an orthodontic therapist, the practice manager and two receptionists. A patient phones to ask whether she can book with the hygienist without seeing a dentist first. Who on this team must be GDC-registered, and what can the patient be told?

teach.body: The General Dental Council (GDC) registers dental professionals under seven titles: dentist, dental nurse, dental hygienist, dental therapist, orthodontic therapist, dental technician and clinical dental technician. The six titles other than dentist are known together as dental care professionals (DCPs). The team also includes people who are not registered, such as the practice manager and receptionists. They are vital to running the practice, but they do not carry out clinical dental work.

children.label: 6 DCP titles
children.sub: Nurse, hygienist, therapist, OT, DT, CDT

children.label: Practice manager
children.sub: Unless they also hold a title

teach.caption: A practice manager who is a qualified dental nurse can stay registered, but the manager role itself does not need registration.

head: Title
Main role
Direct Access?
rows: Diagnoses, plans and provides the full range of care
Chairside support, infection control, records, oral health advice
As a hygienist, plus fillings and extracting primary teeth
Parts of orthodontic treatment on prescription
Dentures direct to patients with no natural teeth
teach.caption: Direct Access means the patient can be seen without a referral from a dentist. Dental technicians can see patients directly only for denture repairs and shade taking.

teach.body: The GDC's Scope of Practice guidance sets out what each title cannot do. Dental nurses do not diagnose disease or plan treatment; they work under the prescription, direction or delegation of a dentist or other registered professional. Hygienists do not extract teeth or place permanent fillings. Therapists do not extract permanent teeth. Orthodontic therapists work only on an orthodontist's or suitably qualified dentist's prescription. Dental technicians make appliances on prescription and see the public directly only for denture repairs and shade taking. CPD can widen your skills, but it never moves you into another title.

teach.text: Direct Access is for hygienists, therapists and clinical dental technicians (CDTs only for patients with no natural teeth, roots or implants). Orthodontic therapists work only on prescription, and dental nurses work on prescription, direction or delegation, so neither can take on a patient in place of a dentist.

teach.h: When a technician joins an appointment
teach.body: Sometimes a dental technician needs to see the patient, for example to check the shade or fit of a new denture. Anyone extra in the surgery should only be there with the patient's consent and the treating clinician's agreement, because the patient's dignity and confidentiality are involved. With further training, technicians can also take impressions, intraoral scans and bite registrations under supervision as part of the clinical team.

teach.caption: Practices in England are registered with and inspected by the Care Quality Commission (CQC). Wales, Scotland and Northern Ireland have their own bodies.

teach.h: A front door to wider healthcare
teach.body: Many patients see their dental team regularly, even when they feel well. That makes the team an access point to and from the rest of health and social care. You might spot signs of oral cancer, undiagnosed illness, smoking-related disease or neglect, and the team then refers or signposts the patient on. Respecting the roles of GPs, pharmacists, health visitors, social workers and hospital teams, and passing on clear information, keeps patient care joined up.

rows.label: General health

items: Seven GDC titles: dentist plus six DCPs (nurse, hygienist, therapist, orthodontic therapist, technician, clinical technician).
Practice managers and receptionists are not GDC-registered roles.
Dental nurses do not diagnose or plan treatment; they work on prescription, direction or delegation.
Direct Access: hygienists, therapists and clinical dental technicians (CDTs for edentulous patients only).
NHS dental care runs through primary care, community services and hospitals; the team is an access point to wider healthcare.

summary: You can now name the seven GDC-registered titles, say which team roles are not registered, describe each title's main role and boundaries, explain Direct Access, and describe how general practice, community and hospital dental services link with the wider NHS.

A.q: A new receptionist asks which member of staff must be registered with the GDC to do their job. Which one?
A.why: Orthodontic therapist is one of the seven GDC titles, so registration is a legal requirement.

whyNot.0: Practice management is not a GDC-registered role, unless the manager also holds a registered title.
whyNot.1: Receptionists are essential to the team but are not registered with the GDC.
whyNot.2: Treatment coordinators are not a GDC title in their own right.

A.q: A patient wants to book a scale and polish with the hygienist without having a dental check-up first. Which statement is correct?
options: Hygienists can see patients under Direct Access
Only a dentist may ever see a new patient
She needs a referral letter from her GP
Hygienists only work on a written dentist prescription
A.why: Hygienists are one of the groups allowed to see patients under Direct Access, where safe and appropriate.

whyNot.1: Direct Access means some DCPs can see patients without a dentist seeing them first.
whyNot.2: A GP referral is not needed for dental hygiene care.
whyNot.3: Hygienists can work on prescription, but Direct Access means they don't have to.

A.q: Which task is outside the scope of practice of a dental nurse?
A.why: The GDC's Scope of Practice states that dental nurses do not diagnose disease or plan treatment.

whyNot.0: Recording charting accurately is a core dental nurse task.
whyNot.2: Monitoring and processing radiographs is listed in the dental nurse's scope.
whyNot.3: Advising and motivating patients on oral health is part of the dental nurse's role.

B.q: Which member of the dental team can extract a primary (baby) molar but not a permanent tooth?
B.why: Dental therapists can carry out extractions on the primary dentition, but they do not extract permanent teeth.

whyNot.1: Hygienists do not extract teeth at all.
whyNot.2: Orthodontic therapists carry out parts of orthodontic treatment only, not extractions.
whyNot.3: Clinical dental technicians provide removable appliances such as dentures, not extractions.

B.q: The lab technician asks to sit in on a patient's denture try-in to check the shade. What must happen first?
options: The patient consents and the dentist agrees
The practice manager signs a visitor form first
The technician shows a recent DBS check
B.why: Anyone joining an appointment needs the patient's consent, because their dignity and confidentiality are involved, and the treating clinician's agreement.

whyNot.0: Being registered doesn't remove the need for the patient's consent to someone else being present.
whyNot.2: A visitor form doesn't replace the patient's consent or the clinician's agreement.
whyNot.3: Background checks are an employment matter; they don't give permission to attend an appointment.

B.q: A dentist wants a specialist opinion on a patient's impacted wisdom tooth that needs complex surgery. Which service usually provides this on referral?
B.why: Hospital dental services, such as oral and maxillofacial surgery, take referrals for complex treatment.

whyNot.0: General practice is where the referral starts; complex surgery is referred on.
whyNot.1: Community dental services mainly care for special care patients, children and people who can't attend a high street practice.
whyNot.2: NHS 111 gives urgent advice and signposting; it doesn't provide specialist surgery.

C.q: Which statement best describes the role of a clinical dental technician?
options: Provides dentures direct to patients with no teeth
Fits fixed orthodontic brackets on prescription
Places fissure sealants and treats gum disease
Makes crowns in a laboratory on prescription
C.why: Clinical dental technicians can provide removable appliances such as dentures directly to edentulous patients under Direct Access.

whyNot.1: Fitting orthodontic components on prescription is the orthodontic therapist's role.
whyNot.2: Fissure sealants and gum treatment are carried out by hygienists and therapists.
whyNot.3: Making appliances in a laboratory on prescription describes a dental technician.

C.q: Who are collectively called dental care professionals (DCPs)?
options: All practice staff, whether registered or not
Only dental nurses and dental hygienists
Registered team members other than dentists
Dentists working in community dental services
C.why: DCPs are the six GDC-registered titles other than dentist.

whyNot.0: Unregistered staff such as receptionists are not DCPs.
whyNot.1: DCPs also include therapists, orthodontic therapists, technicians and clinical technicians.
whyNot.3: Dentists are a separate registered title, wherever they work.

C.q: During a check-up a patient mentions a mouth ulcer that has not healed for five weeks. Why is the dental team's role important here?
options: Ulcers are always caused by sharp or broken teeth
Only a GP is allowed to examine mouth ulcers
It is an access point into wider healthcare
The nurse can diagnose it and reassure her
C.why: The dental team often spots problems first and can refer or signpost into wider healthcare. A non-healing ulcer needs the dentist's urgent assessment.

whyNot.0: Ulcers have many causes, including cancer, so a long-lasting ulcer must never be assumed harmless.
whyNot.1: Dentists examine the mouth routinely and are well placed to assess ulcers.
whyNot.3: Dental nurses do not diagnose; the nurse should make sure the dentist knows.

reteach.title: Can the patient book straight in?
reteach.question: Picture five patients phoning reception, each wanting something different. For each one, who can they see, and do they need a dentist first?

blocks.body: First ask: is this person on the GDC register? If they do clinical dental work, they must be. Then ask: can this title see a patient without a dentist's prescription? Hygienists, therapists and clinical dental technicians (for people with no natural teeth) can. Everyone else works on a prescription, direction or delegation. Dental nurses support every clinician but never diagnose or plan treatment.

explain.body: Anyone working under one of the seven GDC titles must be registered. Practice managers, receptionists and treatment coordinators are not registered roles, although some of them may also be qualified dental nurses who choose to keep their registration.

rows.label: Running the practice
values: Only if they hold a title

test.q: Which of these roles does NOT require GDC registration?
test.why: Practice management is not one of the seven GDC titles.

whyNot.0: Dental technician is a GDC title.
whyNot.2: Orthodontic therapist is a GDC title.
whyNot.3: Dental nurse is a GDC title.

explain.body: Each title has things it cannot do. Nurses: no diagnosis or treatment planning. Hygienists: no extractions, no permanent fillings. Therapists: no extracting permanent teeth. Orthodontic therapists: only on prescription, no removing enamel. Technicians: appliances on prescription only.

test.q: Which is a boundary of the dental hygienist's role?
options: They cannot give oral health advice
test.why: The GDC states hygienists do not extract teeth.

whyNot.1: Oral health education is central to the hygienist's role.
whyNot.2: Managing periodontal disease is a core hygienist task.
whyNot.3: Hygienists can prescribe, take and interpret radiographs within their scope and competence.

explain.body: Direct Access lets hygienists, therapists and clinical dental technicians see patients without a dentist's referral, where it is safe and appropriate. They must refer on anything beyond their scope. Clinical dental technicians can only see edentulous patients (no natural teeth, roots or implants) directly.

test.q: Which group can see patients under Direct Access?
test.why: Dental therapists are one of the three groups with Direct Access, alongside hygienists and clinical dental technicians.

whyNot.0: Dental nurses work under prescription, direction or delegation.
whyNot.1: Orthodontic therapists work only on prescription.
whyNot.3: Dental technicians see the public directly only for denture repairs and shade taking.

explain.body: Most NHS dental care is given in general practice. Community dental services care for people who need special care, and hospitals take referrals for complex treatment. In England, Integrated Care Boards commission NHS dental services and the CQC inspects practices.

test.q: In England, which bodies commission (plan and pay for) NHS dental services locally?
test.why: Integrated Care Boards (ICBs) commission NHS dental services in England.

whyNot.0: The GDC regulates dental professionals; it doesn't commission services.
whyNot.2: The CQC registers and inspects practices; it doesn't commission them.
whyNot.3: NEBDN is an awarding body for dental nurse qualifications.
